questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

Ms Susan has no control __ the class, yet she is not afraid __ it.
questions.solution_en:
There are certain words in the English language which are mandatorily followed by specific prepositions; 'control' and 'afraid' are two such words.

Control is usually followed by 'over'. 'Control over' means the power or influence over something. So, 'over' is used in the first blank.

Afraid is usually followed by 'of'. 'Afraid of' means that one is frightened because one thinks something very unpleasant might happen. So, 'of' is used in the second blank.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

'On' is used when the objects are physically in contact with or supported by a surface.

'From' is used to indicate the point in space at which a journey starts.

'At' is used to express location or arrival in a particular place or position.

'With' is used to show accompanied by.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The man said that he did not see any chance of success except by bribery.
options_en: The man said, "I haven't seen any chance of success except by bribery."
The man said, "I hadn't seen any chance of success except by bribery."
The man said, "I am not seeing any chance of success except by bribery."
The man said, "I don't see any chance of success except by bribery."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Simple Past Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Simple Present Tense.

Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object) will be converted into Simple Present (Subject +V1st + Object).

For example:

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· The verb 'did not see' (simple past) is changed into 'do not see' (simple present).

· The pronoun 'he' is changed into 'I'.

All options except (d) don't follow the grammatical structure. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The man said, "I don't see any chance of success except by bribery."

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the positive degree of comparison.

She is the most patient person I know.
options_en: She is more patient than most people.
She is a very patient person.
She is the most patient person I know.
She is patient, but not the most patient.
questions.solution_en:
The original sentence is in the superlative degree, comparing her patience to others whom the speaker knows. The correct answer expresses the positive degree by stating that she is a very patient person without making any comparative or superlative comparisons.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Option (a) is in comparative degree.

Options (c) and (d) are in superlative degree.

Note:

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

The most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank is 'blow up'. 'Blow up' means to explode or destroy something with an explosion. In the context of the given sentence, it means the army used precision-guided munitions to destroy enemy targets by causing them to explode. Other phrasal verbs are not suitable for the given context. 'Blow out' means to extinguish a flame or fire by blowing on it forcefully. 'Blow in' means to arrive, often unexpectedly or suddenly. 'Blow off' means to ignore or fail to keep a commitment or appointment with someone. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The army used precision-guided munitions to blow up enemy targets.

questions.q_en:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence.

Unless she/ does not study(A)/ diligently, / she won't(B)/ be able to/ excel in(C)/ her exams. / No error (D).
questions.solution_en:
The adverbs 'until', 'unless', 'scarcely' and 'hardly' are already negative in tone and should not be followed by an additional 'not'. So, 'does not' needs to be removed and the verb form of 'study' be written accordingly in order to rectify the error. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The final correct sentence would be: Unless she studies diligently, she won't be able to excel in her exams.

Option b) do is primarily a verb (to perform an action) or an auxiliary verb. While it can be a noun (e.g., a party, hairdo), none of its noun meanings fit the context of morning moisture.

Option c) new is an adjective, meaning recently made or obtained. It is not a noun and cannot be the subject of "glistened" in this way.

So, the complete sentence is: The early morning dew glistened on the delicate spider webs.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

This also implies that "AB" forms a mandatory pair. Sentence D concludes the paragraph by stating the "ultimate goal" of these rewilding initiatives, providing a sense of finality and purpose to the entire concept. Therefore, the most logical arrangement is CABD.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select the option that has an error.

The new CEO promised not only to streamline operations, but also he would improve employee morale.
questions.solution_en:
This question tests for parallel structure with correlative conjunctions ("not only... but also"). The grammatical structure following each part of the conjunction should be the same. The first part is followed by an infinitive phrase ("to streamline operations"). The second part should also be followed by a parallel structure. The phrase "he would improve" breaks the parallelism. The correct sentence would be: "The new CEO promised not only to streamline operations but also to improve employee morale."

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A) Across the animal kingdom, migratory patterns vary widely, often dictated by seasonal changes, resource availability, or reproductive cycles.

B) Migration, an age-old phenomenon embedded within the fabric of numerous species, denotes the deliberate movement of populations from one region to another.

C) Similarly, mammals, such as wildebeests in Africa, embark on epic migrations driven by the pursuit of greener pastures and water sources.

D) Birds undertake arduous journeys spanning thousands of miles, navigating through diverse terrains and climates to reach breeding grounds or warmer habitats.
questions.solution_en: The correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph is BADC. Sentence B provides a general definition and introduction to migration, highlighting its significance across various species. Sentence A follows the general introduction by stating the variability of migratory patterns across different species and the factors influencing these patterns. Sentence D specifically focuses on bird migration, highlighting the incredible distances and challenges birds face during their migrations for breeding or in search of favourable climates. Sentence C broadens the discussion to include mammalian migrations, referencing the migration of wildebeests in Africa driven by the need for better resources. This sequence creates a coherent flow, starting with a general definition of migration (B), moving to the variability of migratory patterns (A), then focusing on bird migration (D), and finally expanding the scope to include mammalian migrations (C). The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Past Continuous Tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Past Continuous (Subject + was/were+V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

Jack said that he had been going through a rough phase. (Indirect Speech)

Jack said, "I was going through a rough phase". (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect speech to Direct Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
said thatsaid
heI
Had been analysingWas analysing

The sentence that follows the above mentioned conditions is option (a) "The chief technician said, "I was analysing the viral samples"".

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).
